issues.description: The template repository explicitly declares a public no-argument constructor for the Person class (template_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java, line 12: 'public Person() {}'), but the solution repository omits this constructor entirely. In a Spring Boot REST API context, Jackson (the default JSON deserializer) requires a no-argument constructor to deserialize incoming JSON request bodies into Person objects for the POST /persons and PUT /persons/{personId} endpoints. A student following the template will include the explicit no-arg constructor; comparing with the solution, they will find no such constructor and cannot determine whether the constructor is required, optional, or whether the solution intentionally relies on Java's implicit default constructor. This inconsistency makes the correct class structure ambiguous.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the explicit no-argument constructor 'public Person() {}' back to solution_repository/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java, after the field declarations (line 10) and before the getter/setter methods, to match the template repository's class structure.
